All notable changes to **FOS Show Control** are documented here.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [1.0.0] — 2026-08-31

### Added

- **FOS Show Console**, a ready-made desk you drop into your scene: sixteen cue keys with
  their indicators, a master fader, a fade fader, blackout and replay, and the director
  inside it, already wired.
- **Show Director**: a 16-cue show, with a master level, a blackout and a fade time,
  shared with the whole room and rebuilt from scratch by anyone joining late.
- **Show Light**: one intensity and one colour per cue for any of your lights, faded
  by the director. Switches the Light component off at zero.
- **Show Toggle**: switches a group of objects on or off per cue — your effects, your
  lasers, your smoke.
- **Show Animator**: plays one of your own animator states or triggers per cue, and can
  resume a looping animation where it should be by now rather than restarting it, so every
  player sees the same frame — latecomers included. A cue left empty either lets the
  animation carry on or freezes it in place, your choice.
- **Show Particles**: emits for the length of a cue, or fires a single shot as it comes
  up. Stopping ends the emission and lets airborne particles drift away instead of
  wiping them. A one-shot never fires for somebody joining mid-show: a burst is a moment,
  not a state.
- **Show Material**: recolours an emissive surface per cue — neon, LED, screens — with a
  separate brightness so a colour can pulse without being typed twice. Written through a
  property block, so your material asset is never modified and objects sharing one
  material can differ. The cue sheet stores and recalls these looks like any other.
- **Show Relay**: sends an event name to any Udon behaviour on a cue, so the show can
  drive ProTV, AudioLink, or your own scripts without this pack depending on any of them.
- **Show Button** and **Show Slider**: the console keys and faders, with a light that
  follows the cue somebody else just called. A key takes its number and its name from
  the cue sheet and recolours itself when lit, so a cue is named once and not twice.
- **Label the console keys**: a button on the director that writes those numbers, names
  and colours onto the keys while you build, instead of only at run time.
- **Show Readout**: writes the current cue number and name, the fade time, the master
  level and the blackout state into TextMeshPro labels. Every field is optional, so a
  console can carry several — one per display.
- **Cue sheet**: light your scene by hand, then store the look into a cue — and recall it
  later to keep working on it. In the director's inspector.
- Network sending is throttled and coalesced: dragging a fader produces one update every
  fifth of a second instead of one per frame, which is what the manual sync rate allows.
  Local feedback stays immediate.
- The Show Material inspector names the reason a surface stays black — emission switched
  off, a shader property that does not exist, emission baked into the lightmap, or a cue
  sheet never stored — and offers to switch emission on for you.
- Warnings for the two failures that are otherwise silent: a director sharing its
  GameObject with another Udon behaviour, and a node whose table is shorter than the show.
